results.reasoning: Judged against two scratch copies served from inside themselves on ports 4931 and 4941 (the record keeps the target's own base_url; the copies are what governance requires and are gone now), driven through an extension-shaped host page — server, bp: '', frame.url, the shape extension/boot-host.js uses — because the server's own review.html bakes ?bp= from the folder it was started on and so can never reach this gate, and the rule is about walkdown arriving at a page knowing nothing. Framing an ordinary page nothing claims, the panel stopped on the gate and opened nothing: start.unclaimed read 'No blueprint covers this page' with the address named verbatim (query and fragment included, checked with ?a=1#frag), start.claim named both roads to a claim — a screen's app address in a storyboard, or a target's base_url — and offered 'walkdown claims --url <that address>', start.new offered 'walkdown init', and start.options listed what the server holds without opening it. I measured rects and computed style out of the shadow root rather than asking whether nodes existed. The count question is where I pushed hardest: with exactly one blueprint declared the gate is identical to the gate with six (I declared five more inside the copy), all six rows listed and reachable in a scrolling pane, nothing opened at either count; zero is not a reachable state, since serve refuses to start with no project, so I simulated it at the payload level by rewriting /api/blueprint to drop and then to empty the projects list, and the gate still appeared and still opened nothing, with start.options simply absent. Because a count deciding whose page this is has failed here before at the far end — a server that does not enumerate — I ran a second pass injecting faults into /api/whose as well: whose throwing, whose returning 500, and whose never answering, each with projects listed, deleted and emptied. Every one of those landed on the connect gate or drew nothing at all; in none of them did a blueprint's board open over the unclaimed page. The negative half holds too: a page the blueprint does claim (target base_url repointed at my fixture origin, /stand-in/unclaimed-page, confirmed through /api/whose) went straight to its screen unasked, and a host declaring its own bp was never asked. One click on a listed row opened that blueprint's board and moved the frame — one step, as the rule asks; the 404 inside the frame in 06 is my fixture static server, not the panel. A remembered pick opens without asking on the same site but a different unclaimed site is asked again, which is a prior deliberate choice rather than the panel opening whichever blueprint it happens to hold. Copy matches prototype/screens/unclaimed-page.html block for block. One divergence, outside this rule's steps and recorded as an observation rather than a fail: the 'Serving <dir> — every blueprint under it is listed below' lead-in comes from the shared blueprints pane and names the current blueprint's own spec directory, so with six declared it named a directory that does not hold the other five, where the drawing says 'Serving ~/Development/acme-shop, which holds this one.' No page errors in any state. The screenshots were re-driven by a throwaway Playwright script over the same states and the same host pages I drove by hand, since the browser I judged in cannot write to disk; the judgment is what I drove and measured, and probes.txt carries the measurements. Both scratch copies were removed, the fixture pages that had to sit under the symlinked prototype/ were deleted, and the tree is clean.
